scenario_description:
Objective: Add optional neutral language-access visibility to Tuesday’s Civic Center lobby resource table.
Emerging Need: A tentative table gains evidence of multilingual help questions and a usable tabletop-card spot before sign packets close.
Decision Context: A stored materials record identifies the approved card, custodian, wording limits, and release cutoff needed to separate a reversible hold from an improvised sign.
Consequence: Timely coordination could help more visitors notice official language-help resources; without it, the confirmed table still runs with standard handouts.

parameter.title: Civic Center lobby public resource table
parameter.description: Tentative volunteer-facing public resource table with standard county election-office handouts only; lobby placement pending facilities confirmation.

parameter.subject: Language-access question trend for Tuesday lobby table
parameter.body: Desk log summary: seven callers since Friday asked where to find official election help in Spanish or Vietnamese. If the Tuesday lobby table goes forward, neutral visibility for official language-help resources would be useful; no special script or translations are being requested.

parameter.content: I checked the Civic Center lobby layout. The regular handout rack sits past security, so people at the election table may not notice it first. There is room for one small tabletop card at check-in, but not another poster stand.

parameter.title: Civic Center lobby public resource table
parameter.description: Confirmed public resource table with standard county election-office handouts; one small tabletop-card space available at check-in.

parameter.subject: Afternoon sign rack queue is closed
parameter.body: The 13:30 sign rack release queue has closed, and crews are sealing the afternoon sign packets now. Materials not already requested for this run will wait for a later table.
